correctness.rationale: A fixed point of a finite simplicial involution has a stable support and orbit-constant barycentric coordinates, giving exactly the simplicial orbit complex of qualifying vertex orbits. For a matching complex, an edge orbit qualifies iff its edges are vertex-disjoint. Odd height: all crossing-central-edge pairs share the center vertex and are inadmissible; lower k-layer orbits correspond to edges of H_k, while central G edges are singleton disjoint-orbit vertices, so fixed space is |M(H_k)*M(G)|. Even height: center-seam edges are singleton orbits and conflict exactly with edges incident to the terminal half-strip layer, realizing |M(boundary-whiskered H_k)|. Both identifications are canonical under Aut(G). For G=P_n, M(P_n)=Ind(P_(n−1)) and the standard 3-step path suspension recurrence gives contractibility iff n≡2 mod3, otherwise the floor(n/3)-fold suspension of M(P_n□P_k). Independently reconstructed all orbit-conflict equivalences for G=P_3, k=2 and 3, both parities; qualifying vertices respectively 10,9 and 15,14. Finite tests do not establish universal PL topology.
residual_risks: The two-layer/three-layer k=1 special cases are excluded from the originality scope.
Finite flag-complex checks support but cannot prove all base graphs and all k; the simplicial orbit argument supplies generality.

originality.rationale: The fully read published 3×n reflection Lefschetz result gives alternating homological traces and counts of invariant matching edge orbits for height three (k=1). Such traces cannot determine geometric fixed spaces in general; the new PL identification extends to any graph G and all k≥2 and distinguishes odd joins from even boundary whiskers. Other published 3×n symmetry-character results are more specialized. The closest new 2026 nonequivariant 3×n manuscript remained inaccessible full text; it might contain an incidental folding lemma, explicitly recorded as priority risk.
residual_risks: The nearest 2026 three-row preprint could not be read in full; an unindexed general reflection-folding lemma might dominate even k≥2.
The geometric fixed-locus orbit-barycenter lemma itself is standard; novelty is its all-graph strip realization and corollary, not the abstract lemma.
